changes.evidence: The Air Force is a past group told on screen in Black Panther (Shuri: 'Everett Ross, former Air Force pilot, now CIA'); he left it before joining the CIA. Under the settled rule a past group is keyed to the person's first title (Captain America: Civil War) and goes first. As it stands, the stage is keyed to Black Panther but listed before the CIA stage keyed to Civil War, so the stages are out of story order.

owner_calls.question: In Captain America: Civil War, Ross is introduced as Deputy Task Force Commander and runs the Bucky operation at the Joint Counter Terrorist Centre in Berlin. Should that task force be a group stage (CIA -> task force at Civil War, then CIA again at Black Panther)? The screen names the building ('Joint Counter Terrorist Centre') but not the task force itself. Sharon Carter's record also leaves it out.
options: Add [Joint Counter Terrorist Centre, Captain America: Civil War] and then [CIA, Black Panther]
owner_calls.evidence: Civil War: Ross is Deputy Task Force Commander under the Sokovia Accords, based at the Joint Counter Terrorist Centre. The wiki lists 'Joint Terrorism Task Force (formerly)', a label the screen doesn't use. In Black Panther he is CIA again.

owner_calls.question: In Ant-Man, Dave (driver), Kurt (hacker) and Scott work as Luis's burglary crew for the Pym house break-in and the Pym Tech heist. The screen never names the crew. Should it be a group stage for Dave, Kurt (A:kurt) and Scott (A:scott-lang) at Ant-Man? This is the held 'crews the screen never names' question.
options: Add an Ant-Man stage under an owner-chosen name for Luis's crew
owner_calls.evidence: Ant-Man: Luis's crew plans and carries out the burglary of the Pym residence; Kurt and Dave later help with the Pym Technologies heist from the van. Neither film gives the crew a name.

owner_calls.question: Peter's last stage is The Avengers (from Infinity War). At the end of Spider-Man: No Way Home, Strange's spell makes the whole world, his fellow heroes included, forget Peter Parker. In Brand New Day he cuts ties with his allies, works alone, and is called a loner among his fellow heroes. Is the spell erasing him from the team a departure (Independent / left at No Way Home), or does he stay in the Avengers because acting alone is not a move?
options: Keep The Avengers as last stage
Add [Independent, Spider-Man: No Way Home] and left 'Spider-Man: No Way Home'
owner_calls.evidence: No Way Home: the spell removes everyone's knowledge of Peter Parker. Brand New Day: Peter 'decided to cut ties with his allies and fellow superheroes', lives as a lone vigilante, and never shows his face to other heroes. The MCU wiki lists the Avengers as a former affiliation.
